interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT3a, demonstrating extraprostatic extension. Favorable findings included negative surgical margins and no invasion of the seminal vesicles. Lymphovascular invasion was present, and no lymph nodes were removed, which widens uncertainty due to missing nodal sampling. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 15. The biopsy findings showed a progression from Gleason 3+3 to 3+4 over time. The documented negative margins and absence of seminal vesicle invasion are favorable prognostic factors. Countervailing factors include the presence of lymphovascular invasion and the pT3a stage. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are critical missing pieces of information that would significantly revise the prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a range for recurrence. Missing postoperative PSA data prevents a definitive assessment of the subsequent PSA trajectory. The fixed estimated horizon is 52.43 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 34.08–70.78 months; its coverage has not been validated.
